title: Adaptive schema negotiator: streaming envelope coercion shim and header-driven opt-in
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: v3 of the public response envelope introduces a stricter typed 'envelope' for streaming events and tool call payloads. Several downstream SDKs and customers are on older streaming parsers and will break if we flip the rollout flag with the new envelope shape. This PR implements an adaptive "schema negotiator" middleware in the OpenAI-compat proxy that can: 1) honor an opt-in Prefer-Schema header (e.g. Prefer-Schema: v3-alpha or Prefer-Schema: v1), 2) automatically coerce v3 envelopes back to v1-compatible streaming fragments when the client signals legacy parsing, and 3) provide a server-side fallback mode that injects minimal compatibility events when tool/function call streaming transitions fail. The negotiator is intentionally conservative: it only performs lossy coercion when the request explicitly opts into compatibility or when the request comes from a legacy-sdk user-agent whitelist.

Implementation summary:
- new middleware at proxy/routing layer (compat/negotiator.go) that parses headers and attaches a negotiation context to the request
- header rules: Prefer-Schema, X-RW-Schema-Coerce (true|false), X-RW-Compat-Mode (strict|compat-auto|force)
- streaming path: a streaming translator that maps v3 envelope frames to v1 frames and emits legacy-style "delta" tool call markers; when translation would lose structured metadata we include an inline "compat-meta" event so clients can surface a deprecation notice
- non-streaming responses: best-effort schema downcast with a deterministic field mapping preserved in compat/mapping.json
- rollout plan: start with opt-in header behavior behind a feature flag, enable user-agent whitelist for nightly SDK builds, then gate automatic coercion under Canary stage for 48 hours before broader rollout

Backwards-compat considerations and migration notes:
- This shim is not intended as a long-term substitute for SDK updates; it is explicitly lossy for certain typed fields (tool metadata timestamps, internal trace ids) and those losses are documented here.
- Customers must be encouraged to adopt Prefer-Schema: v3 once they upgrade SDKs. We emit a persistent deprecation log entry per-client to the audit sink (audit/compat-events) to surface long-lived consumers still relying on the shim

Testing and validation:
- unit tests for header parsing and mapping tables
- e2e streaming tests with the internal streaming harness (bench/stream-compat-harness) simulating slow parsers and reconnects
- integration tests exercising tool-calls across the compat layer and verifying that the coerced stream is parseable by legacy SDK parsers
- load-test that validates latency impact (<2% p50 increase) and resource overhead

Rollout checklist (in-code):
- feature flag gate introduced and default = off
- audit log emitted on any coerced response
- metric compat.coercion.count and compat.coercion.lossy_count
- canary config for region us-west-2 and dedicated customers only
- SDK owners notified (ts/python/go)

Implementation notes and files changed are listed below. Please review the header naming, the translation mapping, and the Canary scope.

review_conversation: Liam Chen (reviewer): Please avoid adding new global headers if we can reuse Prefer-* patterns; can we use Prefer-Schema instead of X-RW-Schema-Coerce?
Asha Patel (author): Great call, kept Prefer-Schema and added X-RW-Schema-Coerce as explicit override for partner contracts. Updated docs to clarify precedence.
Mariana Ortiz (reviewer): The compat-meta event is fine but include a compact reason code so telemetry can aggregate; also please add a feature-flag metric.
Asha Patel (author): Added compat.coercion.reason_code and increment on lossy transforms. Also added feature flag metrics and updated tests.
Derek Hughes (approver): Verified e2e harness; latency delta looks acceptable. Approving with the canary restriction in place.
release_notes: Added an adaptive schema negotiator shim that can coerce v3 streaming envelopes to v1-compatible streaming fragments behind an opt-in header and canary rollout. Not a permanent compatibility layer — customers should upgrade SDKs to v3 to receive typed streaming events. Metrics: compat.coercion.count, compat.coercion.lossy_count, compat.coercion.reason_code.
